relevance_note: Case report of a girl with LAD-I and two ITGB2 variants, plus family members: 'Genetic testing identified two variants in ITGB2'.
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; values were typed into a Python build script (scratch dir) that also checked every span verbatim against the paper and every row against the schema fields. No table was transcribed by script. Scope: P1 (index case), P2 (affected sister), father and mother of P1 (Table 2, heterozygous carriers), maternal uncle of P1 (delayed cord separation, died at 3 months) and maternal cousin of P1 (diagnosed LAD type I); from the Discussion, one patient of Smith et al. (13) singled out with CD18 ~50% and absent CD11a while carrying the c.119_128del deletion ('ref (13) patient'), and the Mathew et al. (15) compound heterozygous p.Asp231His patient. The other two of the three Smith et al. patients are mentioned only as a count and get no rows; the review of 139 cases (7) is group-level only. Figure 2 legend's 'LAD control: A female relative previously diagnosed leukocyte adhesion deficiency type I' is probably the maternal cousin but the paper does not say so; not merged, no extra row, and the cousin's sex left not reported. P2: the paper ties 'the ITGB2 deletion' to P1 and P2 ('CD11a expression was preserved in both patients (P1 and P2) despite the presence of the ITGB2 deletion') but P2 is absent from Table 2 and no variant string is printed for her, so her variant row has variant_original_string 'not reported'. Table 2's index-child row has stacked cells (three variants but only two genomic positions, 'Chr21:46330218 Chr9:101980411'); P1's variant fields were taken from the text, not by position, and the genomic position of P1's c.119_128del and the ALG2 variant left null. Table 2 gives the same genomic position Chr21:46330218 for c.119_128del (father) and c.700G>A (mother); Supplementary Table 1 gives c.700G>A as hg38 chr21:g.44,901,533C>T / hg19 chr21:g.46,321,448C>T (possible inconsistency; P1's c.700G>A coordinate taken from the supplement, the parents' from their own rows). Table 1 column headers: P1 and P2 under 'Percentage (%)' and 'Absolute Count (cells/µL)'. Possible contradiction: 'normal lymphocyte immunophenotyping' for P1 versus 'elevated absolute T-cell counts observed in both affected siblings'; both feature rows emitted (no checklist item affected). P2's WBC is 138,000/mm³ in the text and 102630 in Table 1 (different time points not stated). Normal findings (immunoglobulins, complement, NBT, adhesion molecule expression, CD11a) recorded as excluded abnormalities under D-27. Ecthyma gangrenosum was not mapped to 'necrotic skin ulcers' and bacteremia not mapped to 'sepsis' for P1 (not stated as such); purulent otitis/abscesses/suppurative omphalitis were not used to address 'absence of pus formation'. Functional evidence: the paper reports no variant-specific functional assay for P1's variants (expression studies are on the patient; functional studies of c.700G>A stated as still warranted), so left not reported. Sibling consanguinity for P2 not inferred from P1's statement. n_patients_reported left null: authors do not state a count of ITGB2 patients. ALG2 variant kept as an unambiguously attributed variant in another gene. ISO onset for '1½ months' given as P1.5M.
